title: Lament
lead: Songs of grief and protest, for the dead or to God: from David's laments for Saul, Jonathan and Abner to the lament psalms, Lamentations and Jesus' tears over Jerusalem.

sections.b: Israel mourned in song. A qinah, a dirge for the dead, often uses a limping rhythm and the cry "How!" (eikh), as in David's song for Saul and Jonathan (2 Samuel 1:19–27), his short lament for Abner (2 Samuel 3:33–34) and the book of Lamentations (Lamentations 1:1; Lamentations 2:1). Prophets borrow the form to mourn a nation before it falls (Amos 5:1–2; Ezekiel 19:1). The largest group of psalms are laments that bring complaint and trust together (Psalm 13; Psalm 22; Psalm 88). In the New Testament Jesus weeps over Jerusalem (Luke 19:41–44) and cries the words of Psalm 22:1 on the cross (Mark 15:34).
